headline: Tupac murder: Ex-gang leader faces life sentence for 1996 shooting
summary: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis was found guilty of orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed the rap legend in Las Vegas nearly three decades ago.
details: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, 63, is set to be sentenced for orchestrating the 1996 drive-by shooting of hip-hop star Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas. He faces a maximum penalty of life in prison without the possibility of parole.
caption:

topic: zahed comments on yunis harassment in us
headline_marked: Govt calls [[harassment of Dr Yunus in US 'Awami terror']], vows legal action
headline: Govt calls harassment of Dr Yunus in US 'Awami terror', vows legal action
summary: Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman says the government will not let attempts to harass the former chief adviser go unchallenged.
details: The government has termed the harassment of former interim government chief adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus in the United States as 'Awami terror' and announced that necessary legal action will be taken.

Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the incident, which occurred at an airport, involved a group of Bangladeshi expatriates confronting Dr Yunus while he was in a wheelchair and hurling abusive remarks.
Zahed noted that while Dr Yunus's actions as head of the interim government may be subject to legitimate criticism, such harassment is unacceptable and will not go unchallenged.
The government is also examining whether there were any lapses in the arrangements regarding Dr Yunus's VVIP status as a former chief adviser during the incident.
Zahed compared the situation to the previous harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhan in Italy, stating that similar legal proceedings would be initiated against the offenders.
National Citizen Party Convener Nahid Islam condemned the act, claiming it demonstrates the Awami League's continued reliance on violence and intimidation.
Nahid urged authorities to dismantle networks of violent activists operating both within Bangladesh and abroad to prevent further such incidents.
As of now, neither Prof Yunus nor the US administration has issued a public statement regarding the airport confrontation.
caption:
The government has labeled the harassment of Dr Muhammad Yunus at a US airport as 'Awami terror.'

The government has termed the harassment of former interim government chief adviser Dr Muhammad Yunus in the United States as 'Awami terror' and announced that necessary legal action will be taken.

Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the incident, which occurred at an airport, involved a group of Bangladeshi expatriates confronting Dr Yunus while he was in a wheelchair and hurling abusive remarks.

Zahed noted that while Dr Yunus's actions as head of the interim government may be subject to legitimate criticism, such harassment is unacceptable and will not go unchallenged.

The government is also examining whether there were any lapses in the arrangements regarding Dr Yunus's VVIP status as a former chief adviser during the incident.

Zahed compared the situation to the previous harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhan in Italy, stating that similar legal proceedings would be initiated against the offenders.

National Citizen Party Convener Nahid Islam condemned the act, claiming it demonstrates the Awami League's continued reliance on violence and intimidation.

Nahid urged authorities to dismantle networks of violent activists operating both within Bangladesh and abroad to prevent further such incidents.

As of now, neither Prof Yunus nor the US administration has issued a public statement regarding the airport confrontation.
